title: Sprint landing and done follow the lanes
goal: backlog.py done refuses an item whose KB-Work commits on HEAD include a code-lane commit that is not an ancestor of the integration remote's main as last fetched, naming the code/<id> branch to merge; /kb-sprint and /kb-item land a code item by sync --push (a code/<id> merge request), wait for its merge, fetch and run done on the merged main, and land content items as today; /kb-git-sync says what to do when a code/<id> push is refused; tests.py -k TestDoneLane plants an unmerged and a merged code item
notes: done does not fetch (its checks run offline on HEAD); the skills fetch first. A merge-commit merge keeps the item's commit hashes, so its KB-Work commits are ancestors of main after the merge; squash and rebase merges make new ones (detecting-mr-merges-in-ci.md:23, :31), which is why git.md names the merge-commit method as host setup.
